key_insight: GNN autoencoders can compress detonation flows into latent graphs while preferentially preserving wavefront features over downstream deflagrative structures.
engineering_relevance: Compact graph representations offer a potential route to accelerated detonation simulations while retaining important wavefront geometry.
method: Encode detonation flow fields into reduced latent graphs using a GNN autoencoder.
Reconstruct cellular detonations in a uniform two-dimensional hydrogen–air channel.
Evaluate extrapolation to stratified and three-dimensional detonation configurations.
evidence_signal: Latent graphs with effective resolution twice the induction length reconstructed the wavefront and post-shock region in uniform 2D flows; at fixed ambient conditions, uniform 2D information also supported wavefront reconstruction in stratified and 3D cases.
watch_item: Local message passing prioritizes wavefronts and triple points, so downstream deflagrative regions may be less faithfully reconstructed during extrapolation.
paper_title: Reduced graph-based representations of detonation-containing flows
